title: The Nihilist Reading Of Teito Monogatari #Shorts
description:
Meaning is not found in Teito Monogatari — it is manufactured for it. Teito Monogatari (帝都物語, lit., The Tale of the Imperial Capital) is the debut novel of Japanese author Hiroshi Aramata. It began circulation in the literary magazine Monthly King Novel owned by Kadokawa Shoten in 1983, and was published in 10 volumes over the course of 1985–1987.

Evolution does not optimize for happiness — Teito Monogatari shows exactly where that breaks. The film received positive critical reception and was a commercial success, becoming one of the top ten highest grossing domestic movies of that year. The success of this adaptation prompted the production of a sequel, Tokyo: The Last War (1989), loosely based on the 11th book, Great War in the Capital.
